thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks On Track For Worst Day In Months As Trump's Trade Threats Rattle; Dow Below Key Level

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks On Track For Worst Day In Months As Trump's Trade Threats Rattle; Dow Below Key Level
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Technology shares hit amid reports of trade measures against China
U.S. stocks plummeted in afternoon trading on Monday, with major indexes seeing their biggest one-day drop in months and the Dow set to close below a closely watched level as fresh threats from President Donald Trump against the U.S.'s trading partners undercut investor sentiment.
The day's losses were widespread, with 26 of the Dow's 30 components trading lower, along with nine of the 11 primary S&P 500 sectors. Tech was the biggest decliner of the day, however, dropping 3% in its biggest one-day decline since March.
What are the benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 420 points, or 1.7%, to 24,165. The blue-chip average was on track for its biggest one-day drop since April 6, and the day's decline put it on track to at its lowest level since May 3.
The Dow is also set to end below its 200-day moving average for the first time in about two years. The moving average is a closely watched gauge of an asset's long-term momentum trends, and while the Dow has dipped below it on an intraday basis two other times in 2018, it rebounded above it both times. Finishing below it could be a sign that more selling is in store.
The S&P 500 fell 46 points, or 1.7%, to 2,709. The benchmark index is also on track for its biggest daily decline since April 6, as well as its lowest close since May 29.
The Nasdaq Composite Index declined 185 points, or 2.4%, to 7,507 amid reports of new efforts to block Chinese investment in and sales to U.S. tech firms (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/highflying-tech-stocks-hammered-by-china-fears-2018-06-25). The scale of the day's drop represented the biggest one-day slump for the Nasdaq since April 2.
The Cboe Volatility Index soared 35% to 18.63, its highest level since April 12, and its biggest one-day jump since Feb. 5.
Read:Stock-market leaders yet to be undercut by trade-war fears (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-leaders-yet-to-be-undercut-by-trade-war-fears-2018-06-23)
What's driving markets?
Trade hostilities were once again weighing on U.S. stock-market indexes. In a Twitter post on Sunday, Trump called on trading partners (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trumps-latest-threat-to-us-trade-partners-drop-tariffs-or-face-consequences-2018-06-24) to remove their "trade barriers and tariffs or be met with more reciprocity by the U.S."
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1010978975391322112)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/and-the-most-american-made-car-is-2018-06-21)That tweet may be aimed at the European Union, which on Friday began implementing tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/eu-to-impose-tariffs-on-32-billion-of-us-goods-starting-friday-2018-06-20) on $3.2 billion in U.S. imports. The president responded by threatening 20% tariffs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-today-president-threatens-tariffs-on-european-cars-tells-republicans-to-stop-wasting-their-time-on-immigration-2018-06-22) on European cars entering the U.S.
Check out:How Trump's European auto tariff proposal could backfire (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-trumps-european-auto-tariff-proposal-could-backfire-2018-06-22)
China has also been in the firing line, and by the end of the week, Trump is expected to announce curbs on Chinese investment in U.S. technology firms (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-seeks-curbs-on-chinese-investment-in-us-tech-firms-exports-to-china-2018-06-24) and bars on further additional tech exports to Beijing (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-seeks-curbs-on-chinese-investment-in-us-tech-firms-exports-to-china-2018-06-24). Trump has already threatened more retaliatory levies against China imports, if that country attempts its own tariff response.
On Sunday, the People's Bank of China said Sunday it would reduce the amount of reserves banks are required to keep with the central bank, which would free up more than $100 billion for commercial banks to boost lending and restructure debt.
Signs of a prolonged trade war took a toll on stocks last week, as investors grow increasingly concerned that the global economy could take a hit from those tensions.
Don't miss:Why a major trade war could mean a 'full-blown recession' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-a-major-trade-war-could-mean-a-full-blown-recession-2018-06-22)
What analysts are saying?
"You can make the case now that we're in a trade war. The language has gotten bad enough, companies are saying the issue is impacting them, and there's a sense that the numbers and scope of the issue are ratcheting up," said Willie Delwiche, investment strategist at Robert W. Baird.
"Investors are shooting first and asking questions later, but I don't think they're overreacting, necessarily. Having the Dow close below its 200-day is not a good development. Plus you're seeing bond yields move down and copper falling recently. Both of those could be a sign that there aren't just concerns about trade, but also about growth going forward."
How are other markets performing?
International benchmark Brent oil was down $1.33, or 1.8%, to $74.00 a barrel on Monday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/brent-slides-after-opec-lifts-output-caps-2018-06-25).
On Saturday, Russia said it would back an Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries plan put forward by Saudi Arabia to increase global oil production by 1 million barrels a day, starting next month.
Read:U.S. shale companies may benefit from OPEC's output boost (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-shale-companies-may-benefit-from-opecs-output-boost-2018-06-24)
See:5 things investors need to know about OPEC's decision to lift oil output (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/5-things-investors-need-to-know-about-opecs-decision-to-lift-oil-output-2018-06-22)
Gold futures were modestly lower at $1,270.30 an ounce. European stocks dropped sharply on trade worries (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-drop-sharply-as-trade-fears-lead-to-dark-mood-2018-06-25), while Asian markets finished lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stocks-in-china-rise-but-other-asian-markets-mostly-lower-2018-06-24) for largely the same reason.
The ICE U.S. Dollar Index was slightly lower at 94.369.
What stocks are in focus?
The day's losses were widespread, but technology stocks plunged. Apple Inc. (AAPL) fell 2% while Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) was down 3.8% and Facebook Inc. (FB) lost 3.8%. Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) was down 2.8%.
Industrial stocks were also among the biggest decliners of the day. Boeing Co. (BA) shed 2.8% and Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) lost 2.9%.
Shares of Carnival Corp.(CCL) sank 7.8% after the cruise ship operator beat fiscal second-quarter profit expectations, but cut its full-year outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/carnival-slammed-by-lowered-guidance-2018-06-25).
Rivals Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd(RCL) and Norwegian Cruise Line Holding Ltd (NCLH) also fell sharply, down 5.6% and 7% respectively.
Shares of Harley-Davidson Inc.(HOG) declined by 6.8% after the motorcycle maker said EU tariffs on the company's motorcycles increased to 31% from 6% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/harley-davidsons-stock-sinks-sees-eu-tariffs-adding-2200-to-average-motorcycle-cost-2018-06-25), and will raise the cost of the average motorcycle to the EU from the U.S. by about $2,200.
Education Realty Trust Inc.(EDR) shares rose 1.5% after the owner of college housing communities said it has entered into a definitive merger agreement (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/education-realty-trust-agrees-to-greystar-led-46-bln-takeover-2018-06-25) to be bought by the newly formed Greystar Student Housing Growth and Income Fund, LP. in an all-cash deal valued at around $4.6 billion, including debt.
TV station operator Gray Television Inc.(GTN) soared 12% after announcing it has reached an agreement to buy employee-owned local media company Raycom Media Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gray-television-to-buy-raycom-media-in-a-36-billion-deal-2018-06-25). in a deal valued at $3.65 billion, including $100 million of Raycom cash.
Shares of General Electric Co.(GE) were off 1.6% after a report that the conglomerate is nearing a deal to sell its industrial-engine unit for $3 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ge-nears-3-billion-deal-to-sell-off-industrial-engine-unit-2018-06-24) to private-equity firm Advent International. GE also ends its tenure as a Dow component at the end of Mondays' regular session.
Semiconductor stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chip-stocks-slammed-after-trump-targets-chinese-investment-2018-06-25), as measured by the iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), plunged 3.5% morning after reports that President Donald Trump hopes to announce further restrictions on Chinese investment in U.S. tech companies.
Shares of Micron Technology Inc. (MU) lost 6.7% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) slid about 5%.
Read:China's Meituan-Dianping files for IPO, seeking valuation of more than $60 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-meituan-dianping-files-for-ipo-seeking-valuation-of-more-than-60-billion-2018-06-24)
Economic reports
The Chicago Fed national activity index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chicago-feds-may-national-economic-index-retreats-into-negative-as-factories-slowed-2018-06-25)for May fell to -0.15 in May from +0.42 in April.
New-home sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/new-home-sales-rebound-in-may-2018-06-25) ran at a seasonally adjusted annual 689,000 rate in May, beating consensus estimate of 668,000. The median sales price in May was $313,000, 3.3% lower than a year ago.
